subject: Staged commitment & training cadence — Post-signature MAP (StratusCare)
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@stratuscare.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@stratuscare.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-signature MAP — staging & training cadence

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier this week. As discussed, I've attached our initial mutual action plan (MAP) draft so we can lock down the post-signature milestones: pilot/canary week, migration windows, and training cadence for the three pilot sites. High level asks from our side:

- Pilot (canary) target week: ideally the week of July 21 (we can be flexible by a few days)
- Migration window preference: weekends, but open to short nightly windows if needed for zero-downtime migration
- Training: 2 x 90-minute sessions (admin + end-user) plus one follow-up Q&A in week 2 after pilot go-live

I've attached a PDF with our proposed timelines and a short list of evaluation metrics we'd like to use in the canary (latency at 95th, error rate, and qualitative correctness checks tied to 10 canonical prompts). Please review and let me know any constraints on Redwood's side that would affect these dates.

Thanks,
Laura Chen
Head of Integrations
StratusCare

Attachment: stratuscare_map_v1.pdf (application/pdf, 220 KB)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@stratuscare.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@stratuscare.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Jul 2025 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-signature MAP — staging & training cadence

Hi Laura — thanks for the MAP draft and the clarity on metrics. We can absolutely support a staged rollout with a weekend-first migration approach and the pilot week you suggested. A few notes and proposed commitments from our side: 

- Canary approach: 1 pilot site (Site A) for 72 hours with staggered ramp (10% -> 50% -> 100%) over three days. Canary gating: 95th latency < 450ms AND no regression in prompt-level precision on the 10 canonical prompts.
- Migration: we recommend a controlled weekend cut (Fri 10pm — Sat 3am) for the full dataset sync + final switch. Nightly incremental syncs prior to the weekend reduce RTO.
- Training: we can deliver two live sessions (Admin + End-users) during the pilot prep week and a 60-minute follow-up office hour 5 days after go-live.
- Evaluation plan: we'll run an automated token-level cost/latency report and a human qualitative pass on the canonical prompts during the canary. We'll attach a short evaluation metrics template for you to review.

I'll attach the Redwood-side checklist and a short runbook for the canary gating. Marissa, Vivek — please see below for gaps and ops asks.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_canary_runbook.md (text/markdown, 12 KB)

Soojin / team — quickly from delivery perspective:

- Ownering: I'll be the implementation lead for the canary execution. I'll coordinate runbook rehearsals and pre-cutover validation.
- Canary gates (proposed):
  * Health: <1% request errors for 24h window
  * Latency: p95 < 450ms for 6h rolling window
  * Quality: no more than 2/10 prompts showing regression compared to baseline human eval
- Eval artifacts: sending you the metrics template we use to accept canary (attached). Please populate the customer-side expected thresholds for the 10 canonical prompts.
- Migration notes: incremental weekly syncs for two weeks leading into the canary; final cutover on the selected weekend. We'll perform a dry-run migration one week prior to canary (no traffic) to validate tooling.

Action items for Laura/Tom: confirm pilot site (Site A) and confirm whether there are any blackout dates in July.

Marissa Cole
Implementation Manager, Redwood Inference

Thanks — this looks good. A couple quick clarifying Qs: 

1) Pilot site: Site A is confirmed on our end. We have a maintenance freeze the weekend of July 19-20, so canary week of July 21 works better (pilot prep week July 14).
2) Migration window: the final weekend cut is OK but we need a clear rollback playbook in case of data mismatch. Can you confirm Redwood's expected RPO/RTO for the migration approach you outlined?

If we can get a dry-run on July 12 (non-production, no traffic) to validate scripts, that would be ideal. Also – will the training sessions be recorded? We have several regional clinicians who can't make live times.

Tom

StratusCare

Subject: Final: Commitment and pre-cutover checklist

Thanks everyone — quick checklist and confirmations before we lock dates: 

- Pilot prep week: July 14 (dry-run scripts on July 12 confirmed by Tom)
- Canary (pilot) week: July 21 — run the 72-hour staggered ramp for Site A
- Final migration: weekend of July 26 (Fri 22:00 -> Sat 03:00 local timezone) — fallback plan: revert DNS and re-run incremental sync; expected RTO target 2 hours for traffic cutover, RPO target near zero with incremental syncs in place.
- Training: two live sessions during prep week (recordings to be shared within 24 hours); 60-min follow-up office hour on July 28
- Evaluation: Marissa will own acceptance metrics; customer to complete the evaluation_metrics.xlsx with thresholds by July 10
- Ops escalation: Redwood on-call will be present during canary and migration; we'll run a cross-team run-through on July 15 at 11:00 PDT.

Attachments: migration_runbook.md (text/markdown, 8 KB)

Next steps: Laura/Tom — confirm you can complete the evaluation thresholds in the spreadsheet by July 10 and confirm the July 12 dry-run window. Once confirmed, we'll publish a locked MAP and DocuSign the minor SOW amendment for the pilot scope.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
